comment: THE DURABLE MANIFEST OF THE REPO-BUILT CLOSURE (PROVENANCE-PLAN P0,
which is PARTIAL -- read PORTABILITY below before calling this file
portable).  Supersedes /tmp/manifest_cpmv.json, which was the only
thing keeping the borrowed host binaries out of a boot and which the
OS will eventually delete.  This file is that closure as a property
of the repository.
WHAT IS STAGED.  The repo-built libSystem closure: ../../Libraries/
Libsystem/libSystem.B.dylib as the root, its 29 LC_LOAD_DYLIB /
LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB / LC_LOAD_UPWARD_DYLIB members under usr/lib/system/, the
source-built MH_DYLINKER at usr/lib/dyld, the apple-free EFI loader, the
kernel, and the dylib-linked core utilities built from BSD/bin/.
PORTABILITY (P0) -- RELATIVE, NOT RELOCATABLE.  Read this before calling
the manifest portable.
Every entry here is a path relative to tools/bootlab, which is how
mkimage.py resolves "file".  The /tmp original this was derived from
pinned 38 entries to /Users/max/Projects/build/... -- this machine's build
tree -- which would have baked a personal absolute path into the repo.  That
part is fixed: there are 0 absolute paths here.
PORTABILITY (P0) -- CLOSED. Read this before changing any entry below.
Every entry here is a path relative to tools/bootlab, which is how
mkimage.py resolves "file". The /tmp original this was derived from pinned 38
entries to /Users/max/Projects/build/... -- this machine's build tree --
which would have baked a personal absolute path into the repo.
* 24 members that were named by their $RAVYN_SDKROOT path are named by the
byte-identical repo build product. Verified byte-for-byte at authoring
time (cmp); the SDK copy is an install of the same file.
* libunwind.dylib is repo-built by Libraries/Libsystem/Makefile's
libunwind.dylib target, from the tracked LLVM sources under
Developer/Default.xctoolchain/llvm/libunwind. That target used to write
STRAIGHT to ${RAVYN_SDKROOT}/usr/lib/system/, which made the SDK the
build OUTPUT directory and is why this entry could not be named without
escaping the repo. It now links into ${.CURDIR} and `cp`s to the SDK as
an install step, like every other member here. LC_ID_DYLIB
current_version is 35.4.0, matching -Wl,-current_version,35.4.
* libcompiler_rt.dylib NOW HAS A PRODUCER, which it did not have at all
until 2026-10-02. Libraries/Libsystem/Makefile's libcompiler_rt.dylib
target builds it from 170 vendored translation units under
Developer/Default.xctoolchain/llvm/compiler-rt/lib/builtins and installs
it to the SDK. Before that, Libraries/Makefile's `compiler_rt` target
only verified the ARCHIVE libclang_rt.osx.a and nothing anywhere linked
the dylib, which is why its origin was recorded as a P6 UNKNOWN.
The export surface is not approximated. Measured against the artifact it
replaces: 529 exported names, the identical set (dyld_info -exports,
diffed); the identical 13 load commands; LC_ID_DYLIB
/usr/lib/system/libcompiler_rt.dylib at compatibility_version 1.0.0 and
current_version 1.0.0; and 0 LC_LOAD_DYLIB, exactly as before. All 529
names are DEFINED in this repository -- including the $ld$hide$os10.4$
versioning aliases from apple_versioning.c and the $ld$hide$os10.5/6/7/8$
atomic aliases -- and none was taken from a host Mac binary.
Two deliberate deltas, both recorded in the Makefile: the import set is
29 rather than 30, substituting _bzero (which the SDK's strings.h
declares, and which libsystem_c exports) for the pair
__memcpy_chk/__memset_chk, and _mprotect$UNIX2003 -- the suffixed
spelling -- is what gets imported. Every one of the 29 resolves inside
this closure; verified by closure_gate.py.
There are now 0 entries that leave the repository. closure_gate.py's
relocatability preflight passes with nothing to name.
* work/* entries are build products (see KEEP_dynutils_20261001_build_
closure.txt and build_init_shell.sh / build_applefree.sh).
PROVENANCE (P2).  Zero entries resolve into assets/ except ONE:
com.apple.Boot.plist, which is a plist, not a binary.  There is no "glob"
entry, so no future edit can widen this tree back into the host-extracted
region under assets/usr/lib/system/ the way manifest_dynamic.json's glob
did.  Verified:
python3 closure_check.py manifest_cpmv.json --nm-check 0
-> 0 unstaged dependencies, 0 REJECT, 0 unresolved, HOST-EXTRACTED 0
and the same verdict against the BYTES read back out of a built image
(closure_check.py --image ...).
NOTE ON THE PID 1.  sbin/launchd here is work/launchd, the real
launchd from Libraries/launchd built by build_launchd.sh -- a dylib-linked
MH_EXECUTE against /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib.  It REPLACES the static
work/init_shell PID 1, which merely execve()'d the dylib-linked /bin/sh.
Note the consequence: PID 1 is no longer dyld-free, so it now depends on
usr/lib/dyld and the whole libSystem closure resolving at boot, where
init_shell depended on none of it.  The dynamic-userland ECHO gate keeps
manifest_dynamic.json's own init_exec PID 1; only the library closure
below usr/lib/system/ is shared between the two.
GUI ADDENDUM (make_gui_manifest.py): the cpmv entry that staged
System/Library/CoreServices/WindowServer.app as work/WindowServer.app.tar.gz
is dropped -- a gzip tarball at the path launchd execs cannot run, and no
framework dylibs were staged.  This manifest stages the real bundle tree
(every regular file, symlinks flattened) plus WindowServer's transitive
dylib closure at Darwin install paths, plus the Dock/Filer LaunchAgents.
It also emits the var/tmp/private directory tree launchd needs: with
no /var/log a job's stdio redirect cannot be opened and the job does
not start, and syslogd cannot bind /var/run/log.

#!/bin/sh
# ravynOS /etc/bootstrap
#
# launchctl's System session calls this before loading LaunchDaemons
# (BSD/bin/launchctl/launchctl.c: system_specific_bootstrap() ->
# system("/etc/bootstrap")).  It is the pre-daemon system setup hook.
#
# ravynOS boots from a pre-built image whose root is already mounted and
# configured, so there is no filesystem to check or mount here (no zfs, no
# fsck).  The only runtime state that can go stale across a reboot is the
# nologin marker and the WindowServer rendezvous file, so clear those and
# return success.
echo "-=- Bootstrap running -=-"
rm -f /var/run/nologin /var/run/windowserver
echo "-=- Bootstrap complete -=-"
exit 0
files.comment: system bootstrap, run by launchctl's System session before LaunchDaemons

#!/bin/sh
# ravynOS /etc/rc
#
# launchctl's System session runs this once the LaunchDaemons are loaded
# (BSD/bin/launchctl/launchctl.c: runcom() -> execl(/bin/sh, "sh", "/etc/rc")).
# It is the BSD "runcom" phase: post-daemon system configuration.
#
# On ravynOS the root is a pre-built image: the filesystems are already
# mounted, there is no fsck, and hostname/network/console settings are applied
# by launchd or compiled in.  There is genuinely nothing to configure at this
# phase, so this script reports that it ran and returns success.  Add rc-time
# setup here if ravynOS ever needs it; keep the exit status 0 so the System
# session completes and the agent scan (Dock, Filer) runs.
echo "-=- rc complete -=-"
exit 0
files.comment: system rc, run by launchctl's System session after LaunchDaemons
